title: Exploring the Influence of ESG Activities on Organizational Citizenship Behavior in IT Manufacturing Companies: Mediating Effects of Organizational Commitment and Identification
content:
This study investigates how organizational members’ perceptions of their company’s environmental, social, and governance initiatives influence their levels of commitment, identification, and citizenship behaviors, and assesses whether commitment and identification mediate the relationship between ESG activities and organizational citizenship behavior. It also examines whether the relationship between perceived ESG initiatives and organizational citizenship behavior is moderated by generational cohort, comparing members of the MZ generation with their older generation. 
 For the empirical analysis of this study, the research hypotheses were verified based on 374 questionnaires sampled from organizational members of IT manufacturing companies. 
 The results of the empirical analysis are as follows. First, in the analysis of the influence of ESG activities on organizational commitment, the environmental (E) factor was found to have a negative (-) influence, while the social (S) factor and the governance (G) factor had a statistically significant positive (+) influence. Second, in the analysis of the influence of ESG activities on organizational identification, the environmental (E) factor and the governance (G) factor were found to have a significant positive (+) influence. Third, the results of examining the impact of organizational commitment perceived by organizational members of IT manufacturing companies on organizational citizenship behavior showed a positive (+) impact. Fourth, the impact of organizational identification on organizational citizenship behavior was analyzed, and it was analyzed to have a positive (+) impact. Fifth, the mediating effects of organizational commitment and organizational identification in the relationship between ESG management and organizational citizenship behavior were verified. As a result of the analysis, in the relationship between ESG management and organizational citizenship behavior, organizational commitment was analyzed to have a mediating effect of environmental (E) factors, social (S) factors, and governance (G) factors, and organizational identification was analyzed to have a mediating effect of environment (E) factors and governance (G) factors. Finally, in the analysis of the moderating effect (MZ generation and older generation), it was analyzed that there was a moderating effect according to generational differences. In summary, the empirical analysis results of this study are expected to be helpful to executives and managers of IT manufacturing companies that are conducting or promoting ESG activities.
